correctness.rationale: For Hardy normalized Berezin transform F_phi(w)=(1-|w|^2)/(1-conj(w)phi(w)), iterated Schwarz gives |phi(w)|<=|w|^m when phi has zero order m>=2, so |F_phi(w)| <= (1-r^2)/(1-r^(m+1)) <1 with fixed gap outside every small origin disk, including at r->1 limit 2/(m+1). Thus all near-Re=1 level points lie at small r. Uniform angular Taylor analysis yields 1-Re F=r^2+O(r^(m+1)), derivative 2r+O(r^m)>0, so each angular ray has exactly one small radius r=sqrt(delta)(1+O(delta^((m-1)/2))). Imaginary part at that level equals delta^((m+1)/2) Im(a_m exp(i(m-1)theta))+O(delta^((m+2)/2)); angular continuity gives the whole compact vertical interval with extrema ±|a_m|delta^((m+1)/2)+O(delta^((m+2)/2)). Its positive width recovers m from the logarithmic slope and |a_m| from the prefactor; no claim to recover phase or higher jets. Independently checked nine nonmonomial finite-delta sections, supplementary only. Correct for every analytic disk selfmap of finite zero order m>=2, not just monomials.
